acceptance: Theseus derived_paths entries (exact per-segment file allowlist, required summary path, attested_by check name) are strictly validated: unknown keys refused, entries overlapping gate_paths, .github/** or code suffixes refused; documented in docs/consumer-policy.md and consistent with docs/decisions/0001-separation-of-concerns.md.

Eligibility: every changed file (path and previous_path) matches one entry allowlist, statuses are modified (or added for the summary), old and new modes are 100644, no binary file, and the summary is added or modified; otherwise the plan is exactly as today. Tested, including a conftest.py in a subdirectory, a rename into the directory, a mode change and a deleted summary.

An eligible plan requires only the summary (protected, always required), drops the data hunks from every reviewer-facing diff (DIFF_FILE, inline brief, since-review patch), excludes them from capacity and classifier inputs, tells the reviewer not to open the data files and that the summary is untrusted PR data, and the status description and verdict body say summary only, data attested by <check>, not observed.

The review marker records the derived entry digest and paths; a later round that is not derived-eligible treats those paths as changed required reads, and a carry across a changed entry is refused. The marker reader ships before the writer.
Theseus never inspects consumer CI (ADR 0001 rule 5); no gate change.

BenchBox: build_fast_duration_baseline gains summary (escaped cells, fixed-code rejection reasons) and reproduce (recursive tree, name and mode comparison; artifact provenance via API: ci.yml, pull_request event, run head equals sha, artifact name fast-junit-<pr>-<sha>, PR merged, run succeeded, at most 20 runs one per PR; re-runs check and ceiling-check; runs the script from the base commit). The reproduce job is always-run inside tooling, no-op when the directory is unchanged; a guard test pins it to tooling and to attested_by. The refresh workflow writes and lints SUMMARY.md; the baseline directory is excluded from the docs reference inventory; review guidance gives the summary rubric (block only on a concrete inconsistency); .github/review.yml declares the entry; pinned to the Theseus release.
Required checks core, explorer, results-data, docs, tooling and hold are pinned to integration 15368 on the develop and release rulesets, after the drift fixture is brought current in a reviewed PR.
A baseline refresh pull request gets a hosted review verdict without an owner stand-in.

description:
Pull requests that only regenerate data files (the weekly fast-tier duration baseline refresh, e.g. BenchBox #4477: 9 JSON files, 8.3 MB diff, about 3.8M tokens of required reading against an 872k capacity) are refused as too large to review and need an owner stand-in every week. Root cause: the policy can only require every hunk to be read or exempt a path; it cannot say a file is the deterministic output of a reviewed generator. Exempting would hide changes such as the 33% fall in the baseline total in #4477.

Design: a consumer policy key derived_paths. Each entry names path globs, a CI check that rebuilds those files from their recorded inputs and compares bytes, and a summary file (also reproduced by that check) that the reviewer reads instead of the data. The treatment applies only when every changed file of the pull request matches the entry, so the pull request cannot also change the generator, the check or a workflow; anything else falls back to todays full reading. The gate stays pending until the named check succeeds on the exact head.
